Subject: Deployment mode recap & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Emily / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to learn more about Nova Health's migration needs and the high-throughput inference workloads you're running for clinical summarization and triage. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Peak concurrency: ~120 simultaneous requests during business hours (burst to 250 during batch windows)
- Typical request size: 1.5k tokens average, 3k tokens worst-case
- Privacy: PHI in inputs; SOC 2 + HITRUST evaluation upcoming
- Current infra: in-house GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100s) fronted by a custom API, considering move to managed inference for reliability and autoscaling

Deployment options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest to production, no infra to manage, Redwood handles isolation & SOC2 controls at the tenant level. Good if you prioritize time-to-value and are okay with per-token usage pricing.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool for predictable throughput and isolated tenancy; supports autoscaling/burst and is a common step for mid-market teams moving off ad-hoc clusters.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — customer-managed network and key management integrations; ideal for strict data locality/HITRUST/HIPAA scenarios or air-gapped deployments.

Recommended next steps:
1) We should run a short technical deep-dive to map your current inference pipeline and peak shaping to a recommended capacity profile (Marcus from Solutions can lead).
2) Security/compliance checkpoint: please forward the SOC2/HITRUST scoping doc and any specific data residency constraints (I cc'd Rishi to help with the compliance checklist).
3) I'll attach a short deployment comparison (Dedicated vs Private) and a checklist of migration workstreams so you can share with procurement.

Can you do a 60-min technical deep-dive next week? Marcus is available Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Attachments: [Attachment: nhi-deployment-comparison.pdf (PDF, 420KB)], [Attachment: nova-soc2-questions.xlsx (XLSX, 95KB)]

2) Compliance: we will likely need private networking and customer KMS, but not necessarily fully on-prem — is Private VPC the primary path there or can Dedicated capacity be configured to meet our encryption/network constraints?

3) Migration effort: approx how many engineering weeks should we expect to move models and testing over from our current infra? Any ballpark on model compatibility (we use a custom Llama variant currently quantized to Q4)?

Also, procurement will want a rough pricing estimate (monthly committed vs pay-as-you-go) and a copy of your standard security addendum.

Appreciate it — Alex

Hi Alex — great questions. Quick answers and proposed plan below. I'll let Marcus add any technical specifics around quantization and model compatibility.

1) Latency consistency: Dedicated capacity gives the most predictable latency SLOs because you reserve GPU pools and avoid noisy-neighbor effects. Our dedicated pools support pre-warmed workers and persistent KV cache to minimize cold-starts for long-context requests. Hosted can be configured for low latency but is still multitenant; if you need firm SLOs and predictable p99s, Dedicated is the safer choice.

2) Compliance & networking: Private VPC is the path if you require customer-managed networking and HSM/KMS integrations in your VPC. Dedicated can meet tighter encryption needs (customer-managed keys) but network egress controls and strict air-gapped requirements typically push customers toward Private. We have a checklist in the attached SOC2 spreadsheet. (Rishi: can you add notes about KMS patterns for Dedicated vs Private?)

3) Migration effort & compatibility: For the custom Llama variant quantized to Q4 — we support Q4-compatible runtimes; Marcus, we'll validate kernel support and any conversion steps. Ballpark: 4-8 engineering weeks for a lift-and-shift + validation cycle for one model family (including A/B evals), shorter if you take a phased approach (start with non-critical traffic on Hosted or Dedicated).

Procurement ask: I'll share a high-level pricing snapshot now and follow up with a formal commitment quote. Attached doc has a side-by-side (included).

Next steps proposed:
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with Marcus (SE) to map your cluster+model specifics (propose Wed 08/05 9:30am PT).
- Rishi will run the SOC2/KMS checklist and flag any showstoppers.
- I'll prepare a draft commercial snapshot (Committed Dedicated vs PAYG Hosted) for procurement.
